sentences.text: JUDGMENT

The petitioners filed this petition U/s. 22 of the Employees Compensation Act, claiming compensation from the respondents, for the death of one Sri Nagabhushana T.R., during the course of his employment under the respondent No.1.
2.
The case of the petitioners in brief are as under:
The petitioners submits that the petitioner No.1 is the mother, petitioner No.2 is the father and the petitioner No.3 is the sister of the deceased Nagabhushana T.R.
It is alleged that the said Nagabhushana T.R. was working as a Driver under the respondent No.1 company in Tata Goods Vehicle bearing No.KA-51-AG-6253 from 4 years.

It is further alleged by the petitioners that on 11.11.2024 in the course of his employment the deceased Nagabhushana T.R. was sitting on the driver seat and driving and at that time the attached brick stones suddenly fell on the driver seat of the Tata Goods Vehicle bearing No.KA-51-AG-6253 in Mahimapura gate arch,
Thyamagondlu hobli, Nelamangala taluk which caused the death of the driver Nagabhushana.
The said Nagabhushana was died due to the heavy stress and severe chest pain.

It is further alleged that the deceased was getting the wages of Rs.26,500/- per month and Rs.100/-
as bata, in all the way the deceased was earning Rs.29,500/- per month.
The petitioners were entirely depending on the deceased.

The petitioners have spent Rs.80,000/- towards transportation,
death and funeral expenses.
The deceased Nagabhushana T.R. died on 11.11.2024 in the course of his employment while discharging his duty under the respondent No.1.
Hence the present petition.

The respondent No.1 is the owner/employer and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the vehicle, are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners as the said Nagabhushana T.R.

3. After service of summons, the respondents have appeared through their counsels and filed their respective objection statements.
The respondent No.1 filed statement of objections by admitting that the deceased was their employee and was working as a driver under the respondent No.1 company.
Further it is submitted that the alleged death of Nagabhushana was not occurred during the course of or arising out of employment under the respondent No.1.
As such the present petition is not maintainable.
There is no accident or death attributable to any occupational hazard or risk associated with the employment of a driver.
Hence prays to dismiss the petition.

The respondent No.2 insurance company in the written statement denied the issuance of policy to the Tata Goods Vehicle bearing No.KA-51-AG-6253 and the liability of this respondent if any, is subjected to the terms and condition of the insurance policy subject to proof of valid establishment of valid policy.
There is no compliance of Sec.134(c) of MV Act.
Further contended that, the respondent No.1 knowing fully well that, the driver did not possess valid and effective driving license and willfully entrusted the vehicle to the said driver.
Further denied the age, avocation, relationship of the employer and employee between the deceased and respondent No.1 and income of the deceased.
The dependency of the petitioners on the deceased also denied by the respondent No.2.
The respondent no.2 further denied the alleged manner of the accident as stated in the petition and stated that the cause of death is not connected to the course of employment.
The death of Nagabhushan was not occurred during the course of employment under the first respondent.
The death of Nagabhushan reported as UDR there is no nexus between cause of death and the employment.
The alleged income of the deceased and expenditures made by the petitioners towards the funeral expenses are also denied by the respondent No.2.
It is further submitted that the compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly excessive and exorbitant.
By denying the relationship of employer and employee between the deceased and the nexus between the cause of death and employment the respondent No.2 prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed for the consideration of this tribunal:
1.

Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased Nagabushana T.R was died on 11.11.2024 at around 10.00 a.m., when he was driving the Tata Goods vehicle Bearing No.KA-51-AG-6282, at Mahimapura Gate Arch, Tymagondlu Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk, during the course of his em- ployment under the respondent No.1?
2. Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal representatives and dependents of deceased Sri. Nagabhusana T.R?

Since these issues are interconnected in respect of employer and employee relationship and nexus between the cause of death and the course of employment, they are taken up together for common discussion to avoid repetition of the facts.

11. Before proceeding further let us examine whether there is jural relationship between the deceased and the respondent No.1.

if the jural relationship of employer and employee established between the deceased and the respondent No.1 then the point of considering the nexus between the course of employement and cause of death will arise.

12. To prove the jural relationship initially the petitioners relied on the written statement filed by the respondent No.1 owner/employer wherein the respondent No.1 admitted that the deceased was working under the respondent No.1 company as as driver of Tata Goods Vehicle bearing No.KA-51-AG-6253.

14. In this regard if we peruse Sec.3 of Workmen Compensation Act it states as follows:
Sec.3.Employer's liability for compensation.:
(1) If personal injury is caused to a workman by accident arising out of and in the course of his employment, his employer shall be liable to pay compensation in accordance with the provisions of this Chapter:
No doubt that in this case no proper explanation or allegation of any accident.
But there is mentioning that vehicle was stopped by dashing against bricks (Ex
There is no proper evidence to show that after dashing against the said bricks the deceased sustained Cardio-respiratory failure.
As per Ex.P4 postmortem report the cause of death is due to cardio-respiratory failure.

15. It is established before this court that the deceased was on his regular duty as a driver and after loading the goods to his Tata Goods Vehicle bearing No.KA-51-AG-6253 and while returning to the godown along with the goods the deceased died on the way due to cardio-respiratory failure.
It is the contention of the petitioners due to the work stress and tireless work the deceased lost his life.
But it is established before this court that the deceased died while working under the respondent No.1 and while transporting the goods as a part of his work.
16. In combined reading of all these documents it is found that the deceased died while transporting the goods as a driver as a part of his employment under the respondent No.1.
The police documents established the fact of death.

By considering all these points, issue No.1 and 3, are answered in the affirmative by holding that the deceased was an employee under respondent No.1 and he has died during the course of employment under the respondent No.1.

44. As regards the question of dependency Section 2(d) of Employee's Compensation Act defines the term dependant, as under:

"dependent" means any of the following relatives of a deceased [employee], namely-  a widow, a minor [legitimate or adopted] son, an unmarried [legitimate or adopted]
daughter, or a widowed mother; and  if wholly dependant on the earnings of the [employee] at the time of his death, a son or a daughter who has attained the age of 18 years and who is infirm...'  (iii) if wholly or in part dependant on the earnings of the *[employee] at the time of his death,--
(a) a widower,
(b) a parent other than a widowed mother,
(c) a minor illegitimate son, an unmarried illegitimate daughter or a daughter legitimate or illegitimate or adopted if married and a minor or if widowed and a minor,
(d) a minor brother or an unmarried sister or a widowed sister if a minor,
(e) a widowed daughter-in-law,
(f) a minor child of a pre-deceased son,
(g) a minor child of a pre-deceased daughter where no parent of the child is alive, or (h) a paternal grandparent if no parent of the *[employee] is alive;
Explanation.--For the purposes of sub- clause (ii) and items (f) and (g) of sub- clause (iii), references to a son, daughter or child include an adopted son, daughter or child respectively.

The petitioners contended that the respondent No.1 is the mother and respondent No.2 is the father and the respondent No.3 is the sister of the deceased.
At the time of cross-examination the PW1 being the father of the deceased admitted that petitioner No.3 being the sister of the deceased is married and residing with her husband.
Thereby as per Sec.2(d) only the unmarried sister is considered as dependent.
No grounds are made out to disbelieve the relationship of the deceased with the petitioners No.1 and 2.
The Ex.P.9 establishes that the petitioner No.1 and 2 are the mother and father of the deceased.
Thereby, the petitioners No.1 and 2 being the parents of the deceased are entitle for the compensation.

The petitioners to prove the age of the deceased produced Ex.P7 copy of Driving Licence of the deceased which shows that the date of birth of the deceased is 14.07.1990.
The date of death is 11.11.2024.
Thereby as on the date of death the deceased was aged about 34 years 3 months 28 days.
20. The petitioners in their petition as well as evidence has contended that the deceased was working under the respondent No.1 and earning Rs.29,500/- per month.

In this regard the petitioners produced Ex.P10 salary slips which shows that the gross salary and net salary as follows:
Month Gross Salary Net pay October-2024 Rs.26,855/- Rs.17,980/-
September-2024 Rs.26,350/- Rs.19,430/-
August -2024 Rs.23,581/- Rs.22,033/-
The said salary use to be credited to the account of the deceased.
Hence there is no impediment to consider the Ex.P10 and 11 as the proof of income.
By considering the same Rs.26,000/- is considered as average income of the deceased.

As per Section 4 of Employee's Compensation Act, the compensation payable to the legal representatives of the deceased employee shall be an amount equal to 50% of the monthly wages of the said employee multiplied by the relevant factor or an amount of Rs.1,20,000/-, whichever is more.

In other words as per Section 4(i)(a) of Employee's Compensation Act, in case of death, 50% of the wages of the deceased is to be taken into consideration for calculation of compensation and monthly wage shall be multiplied by Relevant Factor as provided under Schedule IV, to determine compensation payable to the Petitioners.
The 50% of Rs.26,000/- works out to Rs.13,000/-.
Relevant factor is 199.40.
Hence, compensation payable to the petitioners would be Rs.25,92,200/- (Rs.13,000 x 199.40).

21. As per Section 4(4) of the Employee's Compensation Act, 1923, in addition to the compensation under Sub-Section (1), on the death of employee, employer shall deposit not less than fifteen thousand rupees towards the expenditure of the funeral of the employee.

Though the Petitioners have not produced any documents for having spent amount towards funeral expenses, Petitioners are entitled for compensation of .18,000/- towards the expenditure of the funeral of the deceased.

As per Section 4 of Employee's Compensation Act, the compensation payable to the legal representatives of the deceased employee shall be an amount equal to 50% of the monthly wages of the said employee multiplied by the relevant factor or an amount of Rs.1,20,000/-, whichever is more.
In other words as per Section 4(i)(a) of Employee's Compensation Act, in case of death, 50% of the wages of the deceased is to be taken into consideration for calculation of compensation and monthly wage shall be multiplied by Relevant Factor as provided under Schedule IV, to determine compensation payable to the Petitioners.
The 50% of Rs.26,000/- works out to Rs.13,000/-.
Relevant factor is 199.40.
Hence, compensation payable to the petitioners would be Rs.25,92,200/- (Rs.13,000 x 199.40).
21. As per Section 4(4) of the Employee's Compensation Act, 1923, in addition to the compensation under Sub-Section (1), on the death of employee, employer shall deposit not less than fifteen thousand rupees towards the expenditure of the funeral of the employee.
Though the Petitioners have not produced any documents for having spent amount towards funeral expenses, Petitioners are entitled for compensation of .18,000/- towards the expenditure of the funeral of the deceased.
Thus, the petitioner is entitled for the compensation as follows:
